inputs.text: Mahama’s rule-of-law pledge is only meaningful if it protects people who lack power, especially when defending their rights is unpopular. Invoking “collective agreement” can disguise whose interests shape the consensus: cultural norms may preserve inequality and shut people out. Rights should not be put to a majority vote; they must limit the power of the majority and protect those most at risk of exclusion.

output.main_topic: Protecting vulnerable people’s rights from majoritarian consensus
central_entities: those most at risk of exclusion
